items.title: New quest: Is water drinkable? (drinking_water)

labels.name: new quest
labels.description: accepted new quest proposal (if marked as blocked, it may require upstream work first)

items.body:
[drinking_water](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:drinking_water) seems to be promising for a quest.

* [ ] Easy to answer, i.e. everyone can easily solve it (from the outside)
* [x] Easy user interface. (quite easy, depends on how much details to be implement)
* [x] Has a useful purpose. (important information)
* [x] Established tag. (seems to be; ~50 000 times used)
* [x] Low unanswerable quests. (i.e. low false positives, as every quest can be answered; at least if there is a sign)
* [x] It can be determined, if the quest is needed to be asked. (i.e. there is drinking_water=no)

It should be asked for [the things mentioned here](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:drinking_water#Applies_to_.28among_other_things.29), maybe only exclude toilets (they are too common?) and some other tags, where it is not alwayss clear that there is water at all (i.e. rest_area/camp_site).

### UI
> **Is the water of this \<type\> drinkable?**
> [Yes] | [No] | [A sign says it is drinkable]

items.title: Allow answer 'Both fountain and bottle refill' for drinking water type quest
items.body:
**Use case**
Around my area in NSW most drinking water comes from a fountain that also has a bottle refill spout. Like this one:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12725310/195488449-fdcda871-b181-4740-a28e-431a1b15d29a.png)
(My photo, and happy to provide to the project as an example image)

**Proposed Solution**

I would appreciate an answer on  the drinking water type quest that indicates that is is both a fountain and can refill bottles.

I believe the correct tagging for this would be `fountain`=`bubbler` and `bottle`=`yes`.

items.title: How is drinking water provided here?
items.body:
implements drinking water side of #4390 (but `amenity=fountain` part remains and may be or may not be a good idea to implement it)

I see value in mapping whether given amenity=drinking_water is a proper tap or just providing miserable jet of water making impossible to fill water bottle.

Also, I noticed that many bare amenity=drinking_water are in various ways quite likely to be problematic (misplaced, used for water taps without drinkable water or inaccessible to public and so on)

see https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/pull/4423#issuecomment-1260759795 for the next interface version with grammar fixed and better well support

items.title: Add "drinking_water" to "Is this inside a building?"

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
**Use case**
I believe 'amenity=drinking_water' should be added to the "Is this inside a building?" quest.
Drinking water is often on the walls of buildings, and thus close the "border". Being able to differentiate if it is inside can be very useful, for example when the building in question is closed.

Total nodes: 330 518
indoor=no: 8 500
indoor=yes 2 919

In my region most nodes are defiantly outdoors, however those inside building areas are more likely to be indoors. Thus I do not think it should be added to the "nodesOnWalls" edge case.

Should just involve adding "drinking_water" here right? https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/blob/6eaf52d3eb7027b8d292f907b2b0b02366120523/app/src/main/java/de/westnordost/streetcomplete/quests/amenity_indoor/AddIsAmenityIndoor.kt#L26

items.title: Quest "Is this still here? (...)" should include amenity=drinking_water
Tagging drinking water source types
items.body:
The [AddDrinkingWaterType](https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/blob/master/app/src/main/java/de/westnordost/streetcomplete/quests/drinking_water_type/AddDrinkingWaterType.kt) quest handles disused elements in a non-intuitive way. One can specify that the source is still not in use by selecting the last option in the list, but I take issue with this:

1. It's not obvious from the quest, that it is currently tagged as disused in the first place.
2. Looking at the question, it suggests that it asks the type of the source, not if it works at all. These two things are conflated here.

So I have two possible suggestions:

* Simply do not touch disused water sources, and optionally have another quest to ask if the disused source is still disused.

OR

* Have a clearer question. Currently it says `How is drinking water provided here?`, I would suggest something along these lines `Is drinking water available here? If so, what is its source?`.

I believe the first one is the better option, but the second is much more easier to do, and it is good enough, I think.

items.title: Drinking water quest should tag `amenity=drinking_water` instead of `drinking_water=yes`, at least for water taps
items.body:
It seems to me that in OSM, we have two ways of saying exactly the same thing
- `man_made=water_tap amenity=drinking_water`
- `man_made=water_tap drinking_water=yes`

An [SC quest](https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/issues/549) is triggered when a water tap doesn't have tags indicating whether the water is drinkable. If the user answers yes it tags `drinking_water=yes`. I suggest it should tag `amenity=drinking_water` instead.

Reasons in favour
- a lot of data consumers expect any drinking water source to have the tag `amenity=drinking_water`: of the six featured layers on osm.org, five will only show the tap if it has `amenity=drinking_water`. Only one layer (CyclOSM) will show a `man_made=water_tap` with `drinking_water=yes`
- in the data, there are 18 916 combinations of `man_made=water_tap` with `amenity=drinking_water` and only 7 739 combinations of `man_made=water_tap` with `drinking_water=yes`. So `amenity=drinking_water` seems to be the preferred way of tagging a tap with drinking water

This would all be fine if there was a semantic difference between `amenity=drinking_water man_made=water_tap` and `man_made=water_tap drinking_water=yes`, so I asked the question [in the community forum](https://community.openstreetmap.org/t/water-taps-with-drinking-water/113778) and although there were voices on both sides of the argument, only one person tried to make the argument that the two are semantically different, but no else one agreed with them. 

The `amenity=drinking_water` [Wiki page](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:amenity=drinking_water) is also clear that a tap that supplies drinking water fits the definition, and the examples show the combination of `amenity=drinking_water` and `man_made=water_tap` of `amenity=drinking_water`. The [water tap page](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:man_made%3Dwater_tap) page is less clear but in all the tagging examples, when the tag supplies drinking water it always has `amenity=drinking_water` (sometimes in addition to drinking_water=yes)

Tagging @matkoniecz who agreed in the thread that this should be changed.

I created a similar [report](https://github.com/openstreetmap/id-tagging-schema/issues/1270) for the iD tagging scheme (which offers both ways of tagging).

items.title: "Drinking Water" quest should not trigger on disused/historic wells
items.body:
StreetComplete asks "Is the water potable here?" even on wells that are already marked as `disused=yes, historic=yes`, so marking them as non-potable water seems unhelpful.

**How to Reproduce**
Step 1: Be in the vicinity of a disused/historic well, and search for quests.
Step 2: Observe that StreetComplete marks the well as a quest item, even though adding such information is not helpful.

The [Overpass Turbo **Wizard**](http://www.overpass-turbo.eu/) makes it easy to combine the quest trigger (taken from `AddDrinkingWater.kt`) and add `and (disused = yes or historic = yes)` to find all the places where StreetComplete will trigger a quest on a disused/historic well.

Here's the **Wizard** query, since the full Overpass query is long to paste here:
`(man_made = water_tap or man_made = water_well or natural = spring) and access !~ "private|no" and indoor != yes and drinking_water is null and "drinking_water:legal" is null and amenity != drinking_water and (seasonal is null or seasonal = no) and (disused = yes or historic = yes)`

**Expected Behavior**
StreetComplete should not ask whether the non-existent water in a historic well is potable.

**Versions affected**
I'm using SC 51.1, but since the query in `master` still doesn't mention `disused` or `historic`, I believe that also the latest version is affected.

EDIT: Original feature see #549

items.title: Can you fill a water bottle easily with drinking water here?
items.body:
<!-- 
Please read the guidelines for new quest suggestions before posting one: 
https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/blob/master/QUEST_GUIDELINES.md
-->

### General
Affected tag(s) to be modified/added: [bottle](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:bottle)
Question asked: **Can you fill a water bottle easily with drinking water here?**

<!-- If the answer is not obvious, please add a short explanation below each item. -->
### Checklist
Checklist for quest suggestions (see [guidelines](https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/blob/master/QUEST_GUIDELINES.md)):
- [X] 🚧 **To be added tag is established and has a useful purpose:** There are currently 13,181 uses ([taginfo](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/keys/?key=bottle)) which is comparatively low. To my knowledge, this tag is not yet particularly used in software, but would have potential for it. Usage has been increasing fast since 2020.
- [X] 🤔 **Any answer the user can give must have an equivalent tagging (Quest should not reappear to other users when solved by one):** It's common to tag yes or no. The share of "No" is currently around 15%.
- [X] 🐿️ **Easily answerable by everyone from the outside but a survey is necessary:** The understanding to tag should be present, even though drinking bottles can be different sizes. Whether a bottle can be filled up there, one should already be able to recognize when passing, since fountains are largely outside.
- [X] 💤 **Not an overwhelming percentage of quests have the same answer (No spam):** From my experience, drinking water points are not found on every corner. There are countries like Italy where there are proportionally more, but even here it is not spammy. Also, I would say that the majority of drinking water points allow you to fill a bottle. So the "no" rate should be rather low.
- [X] 🕓 **Applies to a reasonable number of map data (Worth the effort):** As of today, there are 244,022 drinking water points without bottle=* value worldwide. 

<!--
All of the above should be fulfilled. 
If you are not sure about how one condition applies to your suggestion or you have (very) strong reasons that a condition may not needed to be satisfied in your case, just note that down. Someone else may come up with some ideas.
-->

### Ideas for implementation

<!-- If you have any idea for how elements should be selected, add it here. -->
**Element selection:** 

- [amenity=drinking_water](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:amenity%3Ddrinking_water) AND [bottle!=*](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:bottle)
- [man_made=water_tap](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:man_made=water_tap) AND [bottle!=*](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:bottle) AND [drinking_water=yes](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:drinking_water)
- [man_made=water_well](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:man_made=water_well) AND [bottle!=*](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:bottle) AND [drinking_water=yes](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:drinking_water) 
**TBD**: To enable meaningful tagging, a strict selection of sub-tags should probably be chosen. "drinking_water=yes" is mandatory, but probably others like `pump_mechanism=piston` and `mechanical_driver=manual` is needed.
- [amenity=fountain](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:amenity=fountain)  AND [bottle!=*](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:bottle) AND [drinking_water=yes](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:drinking_water): If a fountain has a "drinking_water=yes", it should be possible to fill a bottle there.
- [man_made=drinking_fountain](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:man_made=drinking_fountain) AND [bottle!=*](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:bottle)
**TBD**: From my point of view, the tag implies that there is only a small jet of water shooting upwards at which it should be impossible to fill a bottle.
- [natural=spring](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:natural=spring) AND [bottle!=*](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:bottle)
**TBD**: If the spring looks like the one in the wiki (a pipe coming out of the middle of the mountain and carrying water), then it makes sense. But I suspect very few springs look like that.

<!-- If you have any idea whether metadata per country is needed, add it here. If you know where to get this data from, mention it here too -->
**Metadata needed:** 
I have made a OverPass query that requests all of the above cases in my county: https://overpass-turbo.eu/s/1jie
That would be a little more than 500.

<!-- If you have any idea on how the UI (the form appearing when the quest is asked) should look like.
You can use any way to propose a UI. Feel free to include a mockup. 
Do include all answer possibilities you consider for that quest. -->
**Proposed UI:**
I would choose a simple yes/no question here and choose a bottle=yes or bottle=no according to the answer.
And I would choose a generic bicycle bottle as icon like this one: https://www.svgrepo.com/svg/73486/bottle

**Impediments to discuss:**
- No drinking water: I would formulate the question as explicitly as possible so that it really emerges that you can fill drinking water into a bottle there. How would we then cover the case that there is no drinking water there at all? Ideally, we could trigger the drinking water quest when the user chooses "Not answerable".
- I have seen some fountains where it would be technically possible to fill a bottle, but the water only runs out in droplets, which would lead to the process taking forever until the bottle is full. Would a new tagging variant like bottle=limited be appropriate here?
